attribution.new_contribution: Original mathematical formalization by Levent Alpöge. Fortytwo supplied the retained FractionalSliceDomains source. Codex identifies the hyperbolic reflection with the previously available involution of the positive/negative decomposition, eliminating its duplicate self-adjointness, idempotence and linearity arguments. It obtains the dual Hermitian coordinate by matrix inversion and the coordinate expansion of a linear functional. The frame column spans and index splits are then direct special cases of the already published PositiveSpanMatrices formulas. The Hermitian form and the involution transport under a unitary matrix by covariance of the positive projection. The real discriminant–norm inequality follows by casting the already established rational inequality for trace-integral elements. Taking real parts of the CM trace formula gives twice the sum over the chosen embeddings. The Gram–Schmidt eigenframe uses self-adjointness of the positive projection on its given domain. A one-dimensional Schur complement is positive semidefinite by its diagonal entry, and the positive and negative eigenbases reassemble by direct summation over the two complementary coordinate blocks. The flow along any complex isotropic vector is a rank-one matrix update with its Hermitian covector. Its determinant and action specialize directly to an embedded number-field vector and to the columns of a frame. The compact-domain and finite-measure holomorphic integrals use a single local uniform bound on the weighted integrand and the Cauchy derivative estimate. The unipotent and Riesz estimates use the common squared-norm scaling law of the Hermitian majorant. This proof retains the prior verified period-span, majorant, and weighted Fourier arguments.
